title: Open Megabonk
text: Open Megabonk Open Scooby Launcher and complete its normal account or free-key sign-in. See the free-key guide if needed. Select Megabonk under More Games . Start the game, then choose Load on its dashboard and wait for the loader to finish. Use Insert to open or close the menu unless you have selected another menu key. Find your controls Self : Hero, Damage, XP and upgrades, Inventory, and Modifiers. World : Time and Spawner. Misc : Progression and Unlocks. Lua : Scripts, Lua Editor, Console, and Existing scripts. Settings : Interface, Config, Hotkeys, Overlays, and Scooby Links. Switch between V1 and V2 in Settings → Interface. Gameplay settings, bindings and running scripts remain available across editions. Gameplay features require a supported game build. If the host reports an unsupported build, use the current release and check troubleshooting .

title: Choose your language
text: Choose your language Open Settings → Interface → Language in V1 or V2. The DLL includes all 23 language catalogs and installs them under C:/Scooby/Megabonk/lang . First launch does not need a separate language download. Available languages: English, German, French, Russian, Spanish, Portuguese, Brazilian Portuguese, Italian, Polish, Turkish, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Hindi, Arabic, Hebrew, Dutch, Indonesian, Vietnamese, Serbian and Georgian. Download updates Click Download / update languages in Interface. The menu downloads and checks the collection before updating it, then refreshes the available languages. Existing catalogs stay usable if the server is unavailable. Keep custom translations Edit the strings values in your local locale JSON file. Keep the English keys, locale name, text placeholders and JSON structure intact. Updates preserve edited files. Rename or remove an edited file when you want to restore the distributed version. Core Megabonk controls and the shared interface have translations. Other game messages and descriptions use English when a translation is unavailable. Item and unlock names follow the game’s own content catalog. Language collection The distribution folder is scooby/Megabonk/lang , containing index.json and one JSON file per locale. The index records file sizes, hashes and translation coverage.

title: Run a script
text: Run a script Open Lua → Scripts . Your scripts are stored in C:/Scooby/Megabonk/scripts . Select a script and click Run, or open it in Lua Editor . Use Console for output and errors, and the editor’s API docs for signatures and examples. Stop the script to remove its callbacks and cancel its remaining owned action batch. Existing legacy scripts remain in their separate runtime at C:/scooby/UI/UI-scripts , under Lua → Existing scripts . Megabonk API 1.1 Use megabonk.settings for the 36 stable feature IDs; megabonk.pickups() and megabonk.catalog() for content; and queued spawn, item, XP collection and unlock functions for actions. The canonical features , events , ui , widgets , imgui , render and engine APIs are also available. megabonk.player() and megabonk.run() return copied player/run data for health, shield, level, XP, gold, counters and time. They return nil when a fresh active-run snapshot is unavailable. ui.overlay('my_run_hud', function() local run = megabonk.run() if not run then return end render.text(24, 80, string.format('HP %d/%d | Gold %d', run.player.hp, run.player.max_hp, run.player.gold_int), {1, 1, 1, 1}, 16) end) Download the examples Status overlay Player controls Pickup spawner Health, XP, gold and timer HUD Download the complete Megabonk Lua reference Accepted actions are queued, not completed. Check megabonk.action_status() for progress. Stopping or reloading only cancels the script’s remaining work; already granted items and saved unlocks stay applied.

title: Interface and language
text: Interface and language Open Settings → Interface to choose V1 or V2, adjust menu and overlay scale, and select your language. Each edition remembers its presentation preferences. See language packs and updates . Save and load configurations Use Settings → Config to create, save, load or rename a profile and choose a default. Profiles preserve feature values and key bindings. The product data folder is C:/Scooby/Megabonk ; keep a backup before replacing shared profiles. Older configuration files remain supported through Misc → Progression → Legacy configurations . Importing an older file updates the corresponding menu values. Set a hotkey Open Settings → Hotkeys , or the settings icon beside a feature. Choose its key button, then press a keyboard key or mouse button. Escape cancels capture; Delete clears the binding. Select the activation mode. Hold activates while pressed; Toggle changes state on each press; Always follows the feature’s enabled state. Save your profile to reuse the binding. Numeric values do not automatically enable their feature or parent group. For example, enable Player modifiers before using a movement-speed override.

title: Spawn pickups
text: Spawn pickups Open World → Spawner during an active run with a living player. Choose XP, Gold, Health, Nuke, Time, Shield, Rage, Haste, Stonks, Magnet or Silver. Quantity: 1–25 requests per batch. Distance from player: 0–8 metres. XP/Gold value: 1–10,000 per request. Nearby XP and gold can merge with existing piles. Native powerup limits apply. Silver uses its dedicated game path. Collect all XP collects the existing XP pickups. Give items Search the live item list, select an item and choose a quantity. Items are added to your current inventory. Native stack limits and challenge restrictions apply; a refusal is shown in Action status. Unlock and save Open Misc → Unlocks and select Characters, Weapons, Tomes, Items, Maps or Hats. Unlock the selected entry or its whole category. These actions complete required quests and save progression without spending silver. Back up your save before changing progression. Existing content choices remain unchanged. Cancel remaining actions to stop the rest of a batch; completed unlocks stay applied. Actions also stop when the run or save changes. When rewards seem unchanged Gold, XP, health or level locks can override a newly collected reward. Disable the relevant lock when checking ordinary pickup behavior. Numeric controls require their feature and parent group to be enabled.

title: Gameplay is unavailable
text: Gameplay is unavailable Check the host message under Lua → Existing scripts and Action status on the Spawner/Unlocks page. An unsupported game build disables gameplay hooks. Use the current Scooby release for your game version; UI access alone does not mean the gameplay host is ready. Spawning or item grants fail Start an active run with a living player, refresh the content list and check whether another batch is busy. Item stack/challenge restrictions and powerup limits can refuse an action. Unlocking requires a loaded writable progression save. Language updates fail The embedded languages remain available without a download. If a download or integrity check fails, keep the current catalogs and try again later. Edited files are deliberately preserved; rename the edited locale JSON if you want to restore the distributed version. Lua script errors Read Lua → Console , check the API docs and use the bundled examples. Player/run snapshots can be nil outside a run or after a stale sample, so test for a value before reading fields. Hotkeys or values do not take effect Check the activation mode and parent feature, and finish text editing before testing a hotkey. A second timer, XP, level or gold lock can take priority. Saved configs can restore a previous value or binding. For account and connection issues, use General help . Include the game version, host message and affected feature when reporting a problem.

title: TF2 or TF2 Classified
text: TF2 or TF2 Classified Team Fortress 2 The default selection for the original Steam game. Retail has its own world and mode controls, including Mann vs. Machine features where supported. TF2 Classified A separate game installation and package. Its host recognizes the four-team layout and Civilian class; scripts can check these capabilities. Remember your choice Choose a card and select Continue . Don’t show again skips the popup on later visits. Cancel, Escape and the close button leave your saved choice unchanged. Switch later Use Game version in the TF2 dashboard to switch editions. The logo, target game and files change with the selection. Turn Version popup back on to show the chooser again. Each edition keeps its own settings, scripts and game process. Switching the dashboard does not transfer profiles or unload a module from a game that is already open. Restart the relevant game before replacing or reloading its module. View the Classified product preview →

title: Getting started
text: Getting started Download Scooby Launcher and sign in with a valid free key or your existing paid account. The same free-key session includes both TF2 editions; no separate TF2 purchase is needed. Open TF2 from Home or Source Games. Choose Team Fortress 2 for retail, or TF2 Classified for Classified, then select Continue . Enable Start game and press Load . The loader starts the selected Steam game with -insecure and waits for it to become ready. If the game is already open, it must have been started with that launch option. Start a local practice/listen-server map. The current native features and Lua game queries require an eligible local session. Press Insert or F1 to open the menu. Start with a few settings and save a profile once you are happy with them. Choose an edition before opening its dashboard. Asset downloads and languages The launcher downloads the selected edition automatically. After loading, fonts and menu assets download automatically. A bar at the bottom of the game shows the filename and progress. Press F5 to retry a failed download; later starts reuse verified cached files. English is included. Download other languages from Settings > Interface > Download / update languages in-game. For a missing menu or a game that stays on “Waiting for game,” follow troubleshooting .

title: Lua scripts
text: Lua scripts Open the menu’s Lua / Scripts manager or Lua Editor . Choose a bundled example such as TF2 Player HUD.lua or TF2 Player Labels.lua . Use TF2 Snapshot Inspector.lua to inspect copied data, or TF2 Capture Protection.lua for capture-aware controls. Examples do not run automatically. Open the script in the editor and select Run . A HUD example needs an eligible local session with a local player; it can correctly draw nothing at the main menu. Use the editor’s Stop control to unload that script before making changes or rerunning it. Open API docs beside the editor for signatures and examples. The website API reference is searchable too. TF2 Lua API 1.2 The dedicated TF2 Lua API page covers player and entity snapshots, active weapons, conditions, vector and tick helpers, settings, custom UI and capture-aware features. Search by function name, expand an entry, and copy its example. Entries label retail, Classified and shared support. One script, two editions Use tf2 in scripts shared between retail and Classified. Classified also supplies tf2c as an alias. tf2.info() returns tf2 or tf2_classified as the game ID; tf2.capabilities() and tf2.has_feature(id) let you check edition-specific behavior. Safe empty results Check for nil before reading a local player or projection result. Game queries become empty when there is no eligible local session, during a transition, or after Stop. Read a fresh snapshot inside each callback. Download examples and start scripting → Copying scripts into an old build does not add a newer host API. Use the version and function names supplied by your installed TF2 package.

title: Menu settings and profiles
text: Menu settings and profiles Use Insert or F1 to open or close the menu. The interface starts with main tabs at the top and subtabs at the bottom; later layout changes are saved. Combat: separate Rage and Legit profiles, with their own activation controls. Set an aim or trigger key and choose Hold, Toggle or Always. ESP: configure Enemy and Friendly players independently. Use the gear beside the player preview for class and team appearance. Item, building and world controls depend on the edition. Chams: choose a target and configure Visible, Invisible and Overlay layers separately, including each layer’s color. View and Movement: camera/model FOV and movement controls live under Misc. Additional controls differ between editions. Settings: adjust menu scale, language and appearance, then save a named configuration under Configs. Lua: run a bundled example or edit a script. See the Lua guide . Retail skins and local inventory Retail TF2 provides Misc > Skins for class appearances, loadout previews and cosmetics, plus Misc > Inventory for distinct local item copies. Items do not become Steam-owned or tradable. Native backpack changes are limited to supported main-menu and local listen-server sessions. Classified has no skins or inventory page. Camera, movement and filters Both editions include third person, free camera, viewmodel offsets, Heavy rev-jump and auto-strafe pre-speed. VFX filters control fog and individual screen effects. Settings > Capture Protection disables and locks protected visual and scene features. Download a language Open Settings > Interface and press Download / update languages . When the download finishes, choose your language from the Language list. This works in both menu layouts. English is included; required fonts arrive with the initial asset download, and other languages download in-game. Language files are stored in your edition’s languages folder. Downloads preserve files you have edited. Use Reload languages after making a local change. Keep your profiles Native user data is separate from downloaded packages: Retail: C:\scooby\TF2\TF2-Base Classified: C:\scooby\TF2\TF2-classfied Profiles, including default.json , are in configs ; UI preferences are in configs/ui . Downloaded assets are in assets . Existing settings migrate automatically and conflicting copies are preserved. Use the menu’s folder controls to locate editable scripts and profiles. Back up your edition’s user-data folder before replacing a setup. The loader’s Open folder action opens its package/cache location, which is separate from your in-game profile data. Stopping The product’s Stop action disables its active hooks and restores owned input/render state. Restart the game before loading another build. Stopping an individual Lua script removes its callbacks and script UI; changes it made to built-in settings remain.

title: Requirements
text: Requirements Windows x64 and the matching 64-bit Steam game installation. A valid free-key session or signed-in paid account. Both TF2 editions are included. An expired free key must be renewed before loading. The current loader and matching TF2 package. An older package can reject a newer game build. The -insecure launch option. Start game supplies it automatically. For an already-running game, close it, add the option in Steam’s game properties, and restart. A local practice/listen-server session. Remote-server gameplay is outside the current supported session path. Edition Expected game process Steam game Team Fortress 2 tf_win64.exe 440 TF2 Classified tf2classified_win64.exe 3545060 Preview support The TF2 family is a preview. Full feature parity and every weapon, entity and game transition have not been verified. Linux, Proton and 32-bit game builds are not validated for this package. Check the selected game’s compatibility after a game update. Continue to setup →

title: Troubleshooting
text: Troubleshooting The loader cannot find my game Check Game version first: retail and Classified have different executables. Close duplicate instances of the selected game. Start that edition through the dashboard, or restart it through Steam with -insecure . Wait for the game to reach its menu before retrying. The game changed after an update Use the latest matching TF2 package. The native adapter checks the supported game build and can reject changed modules. Do not substitute files from the other edition; wait for a compatible update when the current build is unsupported. The package is incomplete or fails verification Use the latest Scooby Launcher, check your connection and retry Load. The launcher downloads and verifies the selected edition automatically; the game then downloads fonts and menu assets automatically. Watch the progress bar at the bottom of the screen for the current filename. If a download pauses, check your connection and press F5 to retry; verified files are reused. Keep your user-data backup; replacing a runtime package does not require deleting profiles. Loaded, but the menu does not appear Focus the game and try Insert or F1. Read the loader’s exact status. If it reports that startup did not accept the session, restart the game and sign in again before retrying. A loaded library alone does not prove that every gameplay feature is active. ESP or Lua queries show no data Enter an eligible local practice/listen-server map and wait for a live local player. Check feature toggles, team/category filters and ranges. In the API, inspect tf2.session() ; empty results are expected while disconnected, after Stop or in an ineligible session. A model preview is empty Preview assets download automatically after loading. The full menu becomes available once all files are verified; later launches reuse the cache. Restart the game and load the latest matching edition. If the preview remains empty, include your edition and the relevant log when reporting it. A language download fails Your installed languages remain available if a download fails verification. Check your connection and try Download / update languages again. English works without downloading a pack. Locally edited language files are preserved during updates. A script reports an error Open the Lua console, check the named line and function, and compare the example with the TF2 API . Check nil results and API version 1.0. Stop the script, correct it and run it again. Script callbacks and UI are cleaned up when the script is stopped. For further help, include your edition, loader message, reproduction steps and the relevant console error. Avoid sharing passwords, keys or session data.

title: Getting started
text: Getting started Download Scooby and sign in with your existing account. In the game selector, open Source Games → Half-Life 1 . All four games share the Half-Life 1 dashboard and this guide. Use the Edition selector (called Game version in older versions) to choose Half-Life 1, Half-Life: Blue Shift, Half-Life: Opposing Force or Half-Life: Source. Match the installed edition. Enable Start game if you want Load to launch your selected Steam title. A game that is already running will be detected. Use OpenGL for Half-Life 1, Opposing Force and Blue Shift; Half-Life: Source uses Windows x86 with Direct3D 9. Select Load . Scooby downloads and verifies the files for your chosen edition, then waits for the matching game. All four editions have free access. Use F2 , Insert or your saved menu key to open the menu. Use Open Scooby folder to prepare and open the files for the selected edition. Use the wiki navigation for setup and feature details.

title: Menu settings
text: Menu settings Visuals Choose supported entity categories, then adjust boxes, names, distance, skeletons, snaplines and radar. NPC labels describe the model; they do not report server-only health or faction information. Materials Open Visuals → Materials . Choose Tinted, Flat, Wireframe or Additive, then adjust visible and occluded colors. Animated chams offer Pulse, Color fade and Rainbow. Profiles, language and Lua Save your settings in a profile and assign hotkeys to controls you use often. The shared interface includes language packs with English fallback. Product-specific strings may remain in English. Use the bundled Half-Life Lua examples for supported local UI and session APIs.

title: Requirements
text: Requirements Download VC Runtimes Install the Visual C++ runtimes before launching Scooby. Choose the all-in-one package or install both Microsoft packages below, then restart your PC . VC Runtimes (all-in-one package): Download the all-in-one VC runtime package Or install both packages directly from Microsoft: Download VC Runtimes — x64 (64-bit) Download VC Runtimes — x86 (32-bit) Original Half-Life on Steam , using the Windows 32-bit game and OpenGL renderer. The current original-game reference is Steam AppID 70, build 15961492. Compatibility is checked against the exact game files. The Half-Life 1 collection includes Half-Life: Blue Shift, Half-Life: Opposing Force and Half-Life: Source. Select the edition you have installed; its game files and support status remain specific to that edition. Half-Life and Opposing Force have passed their native Windows runtime checks. Blue Shift and Half-Life: Source are also supported editions in this collection. Follow the status shown in the loader before loading a module. Linux through Proton/Wine is being tested separately. Native Linux game binaries and software rendering are not covered by the current Windows OpenGL adapter.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Troubleshooting Which games share this guide? Half-Life 1, Half-Life: Blue Shift, Half-Life: Opposing Force and Half-Life: Source belong to the same Half-Life 1 collection in Scooby. Use the version dropdown to match your installed edition. Which files should I use? Half-Life 1, Blue Shift, Opposing Force and Half-Life: Source are supported editions. Select your installed game and use its matching files. Sharing the product page does not make edition-specific game files interchangeable. The Load action is unavailable The original Windows campaign package has passed its runtime checks. Authenticated loader package integration is still pending. A DLL in the distribution folder is not a released loading option. Missing text, fonts or Lua pages Keep the matching module, fonts, languages and Lua assets together. Keep your writable profiles separate from the package and preserve them when updating. Features stop after leaving a map Session-bound visuals clear when their supported local game session ends. Load a supported local map and check the status before enabling features again. Need more help? Include the selected edition, Steam build, renderer and loader status when contacting support. Never include passwords or access keys.

title: Getting started
text: Getting started Get a free key or use your existing paid account, then download the loader and sign in. Select Left 4 Dead . Every valid free-key and paid session includes this product. Choose Left 4 Dead or Left 4 Dead 2 in Edition . Start that game yourself, or enable the loader’s Start game setting before using Load. Wait for the game's menu. The dashboard marks each running game and selects the newly detected game. If both are open, use the dropdown to choose the target. Press Load . The loader downloads verified runtime files and languages, then loads the x86 DLL into the selected game. Start a local single-player map and press Insert . Remote server features stay suspended. The menu key is configurable in Settings; Insert remains available. See troubleshooting if the menu does not appear.

title: Menu settings
text: Menu settings Press Insert to open the menu. Combat contains separate Rage and Legit profiles; Visuals contains ESP, infected colors, chams and pickups; World contains materials and view settings. Movement, Lua and Settings are under Misc. Set feature hotkeys through the gear controls; aim and trigger keys use the delayed key capture. Scale text, the menu and overlays independently, and choose from 23 language catalogs. Save profiles in Settings > Configs. The two games have separate user data. Use Lua > Scripts or Editor to run examples. API docs opens a selectable snippet guide. Folders Runtime assets are installed directly into C:\scooby\L4D\L4D1 and C:\scooby\L4D\L4D2 , with fonts, languages, scripts and docs directly inside each. There is no extra assets folder. User profiles and edited scripts live under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Scooby\L4DDebug\l4d1 or l4d2 . Downloaded DLL/helper versions are cached separately. L4D Lua API and examples →

text: Requirements Download VC Runtimes Install the Visual C++ runtimes before launching Scooby. Choose the all-in-one package or install both Microsoft packages below, then restart your PC . VC Runtimes (all-in-one package): Download the all-in-one VC runtime package Or install both packages directly from Microsoft: Download VC Runtimes — x64 (64-bit) Download VC Runtimes — x86 (32-bit) A Windows installation of Left 4 Dead 1 or Left 4 Dead 2 on Steam, using the supported 32-bit game build. title: Troubleshooting
text: Troubleshooting The wrong game is selected Choose Left 4 Dead 1 or 2 in the dashboard dropdown. Detection checks left4dead.exe and left4dead2.exe once per second. When both are running, your selection is preserved. The menu does not appear Start the game from the loader, wait for the main menu, and press Insert after loading. Restart the game before loading the DLL again. Unsupported game binary versions leave hooks disabled. Features are inactive Use a local single-player map. Remote servers, demo playback, missing player data and loading screens suspend gameplay features. Enable the feature and check its hotkey mode. Download or runtime error Check your network connection, disk space and folder permissions. Install both x64 and x86 VC++ runtimes. Retry Load to re-check hashes and replace missing runtime assets. A failed verification does not start the helper. Text or scripts are missing Check the selected game's flat asset folder for languages , fonts , docs and l4d_pages.lua . Keep the current module and asset package together.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Troubleshooting The loader says Part I is not running Make sure the game itself has opened, not just Steam or a launcher. The loader detects tlou-i.exe . Wait for startup to finish and check the selected edition is Part I. The menu does not appear Wait for a rendered game scene and press F1 or Insert. If an older DLL is already loaded, close the game normally, reopen it and load the current version. Do not repeatedly load different builds into the same process. A download could not be verified Retry after checking the connection. If the release is being updated, wait for the DLL and matching manifests to finish publishing. The loader rejects a mismatched or incomplete module. ESP, weapon or self controls are unavailable Load a save and enter gameplay. Some features require a loaded player, camera, weapon or nearby entities. Read the disabled control’s explanation. If the game has updated, a matching module may be needed; a visible checkbox alone does not prove that a binding is available. Spawning an NPC or infected is unavailable Characters require resources from the current level. The catalog does not guarantee that every archetype can be spawned in every scene. Reset settings Close Part I before using Reset Settings in the dashboard. This prevents the running game from saving an old config over your reset. Back up profiles you want to keep.

title: Addons
text: Addons Scooby can browse vehicles and peds (character models) from GTA 5 title updates. A downloaded vehicle preset, outfit, and custom DLC pack are different kinds of content. Start by checking what the download contains. Downloads Legacy / Enhanced Identify your download DLC vehicles DLC peds Troubleshooting Download addons Download addon vehicles ↗ Download addon peds ↗ Read the author’s description for your edition, required tools, installation steps and model spawn name. These are addon asset packages; saved vehicles and outfits have separate guides. Legacy and Enhanced use different addon asset formats Download the version made for your GTA 5 edition . A Legacy addon vehicle, ped or texture may need conversion to Enhanced’s asset format before it works in Enhanced. An Enhanced asset is not automatically compatible with Legacy either. Prefer the author’s release for your edition. If conversion is needed, use the author’s instructions or the Sollumz Legacy → Enhanced asset-conversion guide . Its CodeWalker workflow covers supported model and texture assets. Renaming a file extension does not convert it. Saved vehicle and outfit presets are different: a JSON / XML preset references models, clothing and settings. It does not convert or install the underlying assets. Check the preset’s model, character and edition requirements too. What are you trying to install? A saved vehicle: a compatible .json , .xml , or .ini preset belongs in the saved-vehicle library. Follow Vehicles . A saved outfit: a native .json or supported .xml clothing preset belongs in Saved Outfits. Follow Outfits . A custom vehicle or ped model: a download containing dlc.rpf , .yft , .ydd , or .ytd is a model/asset package. The outfit and vehicle preset folders do not install these game assets. Install the addon’s assets first Use the pack author’s instructions and a compatible asset loader for your exact GTA 5 edition. Scooby’s saved-vehicle and outfit folders store presets; copying dlc.rpf into them does not install an addon. A preset or model selection can only use assets the game can load. Find and spawn a built-in DLC vehicle Open Scooby's Vehicle menu, then Open Vehicle Spawner . Use the DLC filter to select a title update, or choose All to search across releases. Use Class and the name search to narrow the list. Clear these filters if a vehicle seems to be missing. Select an available vehicle to spawn it. If you customize it and want a reusable file, follow the vehicle saving steps . Enlarge image ↗ The Class and DLC filters narrow built-in models. These filters do not install an addon package. Built-in DLC models come from your installed game files; you do not need to download a shared vehicle save just to browse them. Choose a DLC ped or character model Open Self → Outfit Editor → Model Changer . Search by name and choose a Category and DLC . Set the DLC filter to All to widen the results. Select a model to apply it. Save your current outfit first if you want to return to its clothing later. Use an outfit made for the selected model. Clothing components and props can differ between male and female freemode characters and other peds. Enlarge image ↗ Use Model Changer to select an available ped. An addon ped must be installed for your game edition before that custom model can load. If a model is missing or will not load Nothing in the list: clear the search, category/class, and DLC filters. A favorites-only view can also hide models. Model unavailable: check that it exists in your installed GTA 5 edition and build. A name in a catalog or shared preset does not add the model to your game. Custom pack does not appear: check the pack author's edition requirements and installation steps. Refreshing Saved Vehicles only rescans presets. Wrong clothing after changing ped: switch to the model the outfit was created for, then load the outfit again.

title: Free Version Setup (Legacy & Enhanced)
text: Free Version Setup (Legacy & Enhanced) Using Plus with BattlEye enabled? Follow the Plus Setup Guide for the reboot-based kernel loader and interface-specific menu keys. Download VC Runtimes Install the Visual C++ runtimes before launching Scooby. Choose the all-in-one package or install both Microsoft packages below, then restart your PC . VC Runtimes (all-in-one package): Download the all-in-one VC runtime package Or install both packages directly from Microsoft: Download VC Runtimes — x64 (64-bit) Download VC Runtimes — x86 (32-bit) Need a key first? See Getting a Free Key in the General tab. The free version is limited to solo play or invite-only sessions with other Scooby users. For public lobbies and playing with friends, see the Premium and Premium Plus requirements below . If old settings cause a crash, rename the Scooby data folder as a backup and test fresh settings. Keep your scripts, outfits and presets in that backup. For blocked files, use antivirus & download help . For connection errors, use the connection checklist . The free version runs with BattlEye off . title: How To Host Public Sessions with Scooby (BE Disabled)
text: How To Host Public Sessions with Scooby (BE Disabled) Getting a public lobby to fill up is not just luck - it comes down to a handful of factors you can actually control. This guide covers what makes players join your session and what to do when nobody shows up. Premium: you must remain the session host This hosting guide is for Premium with BattlEye disabled . Premium lets you host public lobbies and play with friends, but you must remain the session host at all times to avoid being desynced after about 3–5 minutes as a non-host. Premium Plus supports BattlEye enabled and lets you play as either the host or a non-host. The free version does not support public lobbies. Compare Free, Premium, and Premium Plus online access → For the Premium hosting steps below, launch GTA 5 with BattlEye disabled in the Rockstar Launcher settings. Premium Plus users playing with BattlEye enabled do not need to follow this host-only setup. There are four factors behind a lobby that actually fills: your NAT type, your aim type, the region and time you host in, and a fair amount of luck. 1. NAT Type Your NAT type affects how easily other players can connect to your lobby. Open NAT - best results for hosting Moderate NAT - usually works fine Strict NAT - may reduce player joins and connectivity Important things to know: NAT type is normally controlled by your router and your ISP , not by the game. Some tools and scripts offer NAT spoofing, which presents a different NAT type to GTA Online. Results vary a lot and it does not work the same for every player. If you consistently struggle to attract players, check your NAT type and confirm your ISP is not putting you behind CGNAT (see below). 2. Aim Type Your aim setting decides which pool of players can even match with you. Free Aim - largest player pool on PC, attracts the most players Partial Aim Assist - still a decent number of players Full Aim Assist - smallest player pool on PC, expect fewer joins For the highest chance of filling a lobby, start with Free Aim . 3. Region and Timing Timing matters as much as the region itself. Aim for hours when people are: Getting home from work Finishing school Already gaming during the evening Good windows to try: North America, evenings Europe, evenings Weekends beat weekday mornings by a wide margin If one region is quiet, switch to another and try again. 4. Luck Sometimes everything is set up perfectly and the lobby still will not fill. You can host a session that fills instantly, then host the exact same session 30 minutes later and get nobody. GTA Online matchmaking is unpredictable, so persistence is part of the process. Bonus: Check for CGNAT Some ISPs place customers behind Carrier Grade NAT (CGNAT) , which shares one public IP between many customers. This can hurt your connectivity, your matchmaking and your hosting reliability. Contact your ISP Ask whether your connection is behind CGNAT Request a public IPv4 address if they offer one Bonus: Use a VPN A VPN can sometimes improve how visible you are in matchmaking. Best practice: Connect to a VPN server in a densely populated area Match your VPN region to the audience you are trying to attract Locations players commonly report good results with: New York, Chicago, Los Angeles, London, Frankfurt . Results vary, but busy metro areas generally give better lobby population. Checklist - you have done everything right if: You have Premium and remain the session host Session advertising is enabled You are on Open or Moderate NAT You picked the right Aim Type (Free Aim fills fastest) You chose an active region and a busy time of day You confirmed you are not behind CGNAT Still Alone? Be patient. Try different combinations, restart the session, switch regions and keep experimenting. An empty lobby after one attempt does not mean your setup is wrong. If All Else Fails - Get Friends to Join First A lobby that already has a few players inside attracts far more players than an empty one. Once the first few people arrive, GTA Online matchmaking tends to do the rest. You can also turn on Player Magnet in the Network tab to help pull players in. In short: hosting is a combination of NAT type, aim type, region, ISP quality and a little bit of luck .

title: Fix “Hypervisor / VBS is running”
text: Fix “Hypervisor / VBS is running” The Plus loader blocks loading when its VBS/HVCI checks trigger. VBS means Virtualization-Based Security ; HVCI is Memory Integrity . Start with the in-app Disable & Reboot button. If the banner returns, use the diagnostic below to see which check is triggering. For the complete bootloader requirements and loading sequence, follow the Plus Setup Guide . Download and run the diagnostic Download check_vbs.bat Save check_vbs.bat on your PC. Right-click it and select Run as administrator . Elevated access is needed for reliable WMI and boot configuration results. Read the VERDICT block and its Source of truth line. If you need help, copy the full script output into your support ticket . The supplied batch file queries WMI, registry settings, boot configuration and the Hyper-V feature state. It prints diagnostics and pauses so you can read them; it does not change these settings or reboot your PC. What the checks mean The supplied script describes its rules as matching the loader’s checks. The website does not independently verify the loader implementation. Primary source: WMI / CIM → ROOT\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard → Win32_DeviceGuard . VBS trigger: VirtualizationBasedSecurityStatus == 2 (running). A value of 0 means disabled; 1 means enabled but not running. HVCI trigger: SecurityServicesRunning contains 2 , and the VBS trigger is active. This is how the supplied script calculates its verdict. Fallback if WMI fails: registry values DeviceGuard\EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity and DeviceGuard\Scenarios\HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity\Enabled . The script treats 0x1 as enabled and applies the same VBS condition to HVCI. Configured is not the same as running. If Source of truth says REGISTRY , the verdict is a fallback based on configuration. A registry-only CLEAN result does not prove the runtime state is clear, especially if keys are missing. Resolve the WMI error or confirm the state in msinfo32 before concluding VBS is off. Read the VERDICT block A clean result from a successful WMI query looks like: Source of truth : WMI VBS running : 0 HVCI running : 0 [CLEAN] Neither VBS nor HVCI is running. Loader should NOT block. A VBS trigger looks like: [TRIGGER] VBS is running --> loader will show the red banner. Reason: Win32_DeviceGuard.VirtualizationBasedSecurityStatus = 2 An HVCI trigger also reports that SecurityServicesRunning contains 2 . The raw service list helps identify the security features involved: 1 — Credential Guard (CredGuard / CG). 2 — Memory Integrity (HVCI). 3 — System Guard Secure Launch (SysGuard). 4 — SMM Firmware Measurement. 5 — Kernel-mode Hardware-enforced Stack Protection (KernelHWStack). 7 — Hypervisor-Enforced Paging Translation (HVPT). CodeIntegrityPolicyEnforcementStatus is a separate App Control / WDAC signal, not a trigger in this script . A value of 2 means that policy is enforced; it does not by itself show HVCI is running. See Microsoft’s Win32_DeviceGuard field reference . If VBS returns after reboot Something may be enabling the hypervisor or enforcing VBS again: Credential Guard, Group Policy / Intune, Hyper-V, WSL2, Sandbox, Docker dependencies or OEM security defaults. Changing VBS, Memory Integrity or virtualization removes security protections or affects virtualization-dependent software. On a work or school PC, contact the administrator if policy manages these settings. Try Disable & Reboot in the loader first. After restarting, run the diagnostic again. Check Memory Integrity. Open Windows Security → Device security → Core isolation details → Memory integrity and set it to Off . Check Credential Guard. There is no universal “Credential Guard: Off” switch in Windows Security. If the output includes service 1 , review the device’s policy with support or your administrator. Check Windows features. Press Win + R , enter OptionalFeatures.exe , and uncheck enabled virtualization components you are disabling for this setup: Hyper-V, Windows Hypervisor Platform, Virtual Machine Platform, Windows Sandbox and Windows Subsystem for Linux . Available items vary by Windows edition. WSL2 and some Docker backends depend on these features. Check the boot setting. In an administrator PowerShell or Command Prompt, run: bcdedit /set hypervisorlaunchtype off Restart after applying the changes. Check policy if settings come back. Where available, open rsop.msc and review Computer Configuration → Administrative Templates → System → Device Guard . Intune policy may also apply. Ask the administrator to review enforced settings. Check firmware virtualization. Follow the Plus firmware setup for Intel VT-x / VT-d or AMD SVM / IOMMU. Ask support about unfamiliar settings before changing them. After the final restart, rerun check_vbs.bat . If a successful WMI query reports VBS/HVCI off but the loader still blocks, include the full diagnostic output and a screenshot of the loader in your support ticket.

title: Getting Luas
text: Getting Luas Lua scripts add tools and custom interfaces to Scooby. Choose a script written for Scooby GTA 5, or a port that explicitly supports your menu version and GTA 5 edition. You can find shared scripts in the Scooby community or get them directly from their author. Lua folder and menu C:\scooby\GTA5\lua Settings → Lua Editor → Scripts Older builds may label the screen Lua Scripts . Install Run and stop Other-menu scripts Troubleshooting Enlarge image ↗ Start in Settings : use the ClickUI gear or the ListUI Settings row. Then follow Lua Editor → Scripts in the steps below. Keep a downloaded script’s dependencies in the author’s required locations. Install a downloaded script Download the script and extract it if it is inside a ZIP or other archive. Check the author's requirements and keep any supplied libraries, configuration, and assets. Open Settings → Lua Editor and select Open Lua Folder . You can also paste C:\scooby\GTA5\lua into File Explorer's address bar. For a standalone script, copy its .lua file directly into that folder. A script may add its own menu or window. Look at its instructions if it is running but you cannot find its controls. Scripts made for another menu Sharing the .lua extension does not guarantee compatibility. Scooby has compatibility helpers, but a script that relies on another menu's API may still need changes. Prefer a Scooby version supplied by the author. Some builds expose Lua Scripts → Other Menus Luas for compatible imports from C:\scooby\GTA5\lua\other-menus-luas . If a script does not work Missing from Scripts: check the folder, extract the archive, confirm the .lua extension, clear the search, and refresh. Start with a standalone script directly in the Lua folder. Missing module or asset: restore the full package and follow its original directory layout. Error immediately after running: read the first error in Console . Confirm Scooby support and the correct Legacy/Enhanced edition with the author. Problems on every startup: untick auto-run and stop the script. If you cannot reach the menu, close the game and move that script out of the Lua folder before starting again.

title: Plus Setup Guide
text: Plus Setup Guide Scooby Plus uses a bootloader that loads its kernel driver when your PC restarts. Complete every setup step in order before selecting Load Driver At Next Boot . Take your time and do not skip the checks. Print / save as PDF Find your loader message Before changing Windows or firmware settings: Secure Boot, VBS and Memory Integrity provide security protections. Turning them off reduces those protections. Disabling virtualization also affects virtual machines, WSL2, Windows Sandbox and some Docker configurations. Keep your BitLocker recovery key available before changing boot settings. Microsoft: device security . The setup in three parts Prepare Windows. Save your recovery key, then complete the encryption, hypervisor and VBS checks in steps 1–3 . Change BIOS settings. Keep UEFI boot mode. Turn off Secure Boot, Fast Boot and the relevant virtualization settings. Follow step 4 , then step 5 and the outlined pictures . Restart and load. Arm the driver, restart, then load Scooby and launch GTA V with BattlEye enabled. Step 6 has the full sequence. Menu keys: ClickUI F1 / Insert · ListUI F2 . Jump to a step or find help Follow the setup in order Check the required settings Prepare BitLocker / Device Encryption Turn off the hypervisor, VBS and Memory Integrity Enter UEFI firmware settings Change Secure Boot, Fast Boot and virtualization Verify and load Scooby Plus Hardware help: outlined BIOS pictures · identify your PC · setting-name reference · final checks · missing options and support . Seeing a red banner? Read Fix “Hypervisor / VBS is running” . Before you begin: identify your hardware Keep this guide open on your phone while you are in BIOS. Take photos of the settings before changing them so you can restore the original values if needed. Press Win + R , type msinfo32 , and note these fields in System Summary : Processor: tells you whether to look for Intel or AMD setting names. System Manufacturer / System Model: use these for a laptop or branded prebuilt PC. BaseBoard Manufacturer / BaseBoard Product: use these to identify the motherboard in a custom desktop. BIOS Version/Date and OS Name / Version: useful when a menu differs from a tutorial. You can also run winver for the Windows build. Find the manual on the manufacturer’s support site using the exact model , and board revision if applicable. Two PCs from the same brand can have different menus. If a field is blank or generic, use the model label or purchase details rather than guessing. 1. Check the required settings This is the required configuration for the Plus bootloader setup described here: Hypervisor: off. Secure Boot: disabled. Firmware Fast Boot: disabled. Virtualization-Based Security (VBS): not running. Core isolation → Memory integrity (HVCI): off. BIOS virtualization: off, including Intel VT-x / VT-d or AMD SVM / IOMMU where present. BitLocker / Device Encryption: off for this Plus setup; see the distinction between decryption and suspension below. BIOS Mode: UEFI. Press Win + R , enter msinfo32 , and check BIOS Mode , Secure Boot State and Virtualization-based security . If BIOS Mode says Legacy, contact support before changing boot mode: switching an existing installation to UEFI may require disk conversion or other preparation. 2. Prepare BitLocker / Device Encryption Save your 48-digit recovery key somewhere accessible from another device before changing Secure Boot or other boot settings. Open Manage BitLocker (or Settings → Device encryption , depending on your Windows edition). For the BitLocker-off requirement above, select Turn off BitLocker / turn Device encryption off, and wait until decryption finishes. If you need to locate the key, follow Microsoft’s recovery-key instructions . It may be saved to the Microsoft account or work/school account used to set up the PC. Keep the key private; support screenshots should not include it. Suspension is different from turning BitLocker off. For a temporary firmware change on an encrypted PC, the supplied notes describe suspending protectors from an administrator terminal before the change: manage-bde -protectors -disable C: After returning to Windows, resume protection: manage-bde -protectors -enable C: Suspension leaves the drive encrypted and does not meet the BitLocker-off requirement. These commands are for the temporary suspension workflow only. See Microsoft’s BitLocker suspension guidance . 3. Turn off the hypervisor, VBS and Memory Integrity Open PowerShell as administrator and run: bcdedit /set hypervisorlaunchtype off Open Windows Security → Device security → Core isolation details and set Memory integrity to Off . If VBS is enabled, press Win + R , enter regedit , and open this path (you can paste it into Registry Editor’s address bar): HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard Set EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity to 0 . If the value is missing or managed by your organization, use the VBS troubleshooting guide rather than guessing at other registry settings. Restart your PC to apply the changes. If you are completing the VBS registry step too, you can do both Windows changes before this restart. If VBS still runs after restarting, complete the firmware steps below and use the VBS/HVCI diagnostic to identify the remaining trigger. HVCI is a Windows security feature; it is not a standard BIOS virtualization toggle. 4. Enter UEFI firmware settings Open Start → Power . Hold Shift and select Restart . Keep holding Shift until the blue Choose an option screen appears. Select Troubleshoot → Advanced options → UEFI Firmware Settings → Restart . If that option is unavailable, use your device’s setup key at power-on. Common keys include Delete / F2 on desktop motherboards, F2 on Dell, Esc / F10 on HP, and F1 / F2 on Lenovo. Check your model’s manual for the exact key. Surface devices commonly use Volume Up + Power . You can also reach Advanced startup through Windows 11: Settings → System → Recovery → Advanced startup → Restart now , or Windows 10: Settings → Update & Security → Recovery → Advanced startup . Save your work first. If you miss the setup key, restart and try again; a wired keyboard or the laptop’s built-in keyboard may help before Windows loads. 5. Change Secure Boot, Fast Boot and virtualization Secure Boot checks boot software against trusted signatures and can block the Plus bootloader. Find Secure Boot under Boot, Security, Authentication, BIOS Features, Advanced or System Configuration. Names vary by model and firmware version; use your model’s manual if these examples do not match. Set Secure Boot to Disabled . If it is greyed out, consult your model’s instructions or open a support ticket. Some models require an administrator/supervisor password or a mode change; do not clear Secure Boot keys or change to Custom mode unless your manufacturer specifically requires it. Set firmware Fast Boot to Disabled so it does not skip the bootloader. This is a firmware setting; Windows Fast Startup is a separate option. Find the CPU / virtualization options, usually under Advanced or Security . Disable the relevant virtualization settings: Intel Virtualization Technology / VT-x, VT-d, AMD SVM and IOMMU , where available. If a label is unfamiliar, open a support ticket with a screenshot so staff can confirm it. Confirm the system remains in UEFI boot mode. Once all changes are complete, choose Save Changes and Exit (often F10 ), confirm, and let Windows restart. BIOS pictures: find the outlined setting Open the example closest to your screen. The outline shows where to look; the “Set this” line tells you the required choice. The real screenshots below cover ASUS, MSI, Gigabyte/AORUS and an ASRock X300TM-ITX layout. Match the brand, model and setting name; firmware versions can look different. ASUS notebook ASUS desktop MSI Gigabyte / AORUS ASRock Tap a picture to enlarge it, then choose Zoom in for small labels. Yellow outlines mark the control or choice. Some source pictures show Enabled or Auto: follow the Set this value above the picture. You can use arrow keys and Enter if your firmware does not support a mouse. Secure Boot — ASUS notebook Where to go: Security → Secure Boot → Secure Boot Control Set this: Secure Boot Control → Disabled Select the outlined Secure Boot Control option, then choose Disabled. The status above it can update only after saving and restarting. Source: ASUS Secure Boot instructions . Secure Boot — ASUS desktop Where to go: Boot → Secure Boot → OS Type Set this: OS Type → Other OS On this ASUS layout, choose Other OS in the outlined menu to deactivate Secure Boot. Keep the PC in UEFI boot mode; Other OS here is a Secure Boot control. Source: ASUS Secure Boot instructions . Fast Boot — ASUS UEFI Where to go: Boot → Fast Boot Set this: Fast Boot → Disabled Open Boot, select the outlined Fast Boot row, and choose Disabled. This is the firmware setting, separate from Windows Fast Startup. Source: ASUS Fast Boot instructions . Intel virtualization — ASUS motherboard Where to go: Advanced Mode (F7) → Advanced → CPU Configuration Set this: Intel (VMX) Virtualization Technology → Disabled The yellow outline marks the setting to change. This reference screenshot shows Enabled: change it to Disabled for this setup. The read-only Intel VT-x Technology: Supported line above is not the switch. Source: ASUS Intel VMX instructions . Intel CPU + VT-d — MSI Click BIOS X Where to go: Advanced Mode (F7) → Overclocking → CPU Features Set this: Intel Virtualization Tech + Intel VT-D Tech → Disabled The outlines mark two separate controls. Choose Disabled for Intel Virtualization Tech, then change Intel VT-D Tech separately. The open dropdown in this reference image covers the VT-d value; check both controls on your own PC. Source: MSI Click BIOS guide . AMD virtualization — ASUS notebook Where to go: Advanced → SVM Mode Set this: SVM Mode → Disabled The yellow outline marks SVM Mode, the AMD CPU virtualization switch. This example shows Enabled: change it to Disabled for this setup. If your firmware also exposes IOMMU, check that separately using your model’s manual. Source: ASUS AMD SVM instructions . Secure Boot — Gigabyte / AORUS AM4 Set this: Boot → Secure Boot → Disabled Open Advanced Mode → Boot → Secure Boot. Select the yellow-outlined Secure Boot control, then choose Disabled. This AM4 reference shows Enabled and Active before the change; Active is a status, not the setting to select. Keep UEFI boot mode. The Custom mode and key-management items visible in this source picture are not steps to follow for this setup. Source: Gigabyte AM4 / sTRX4 Secure Boot reference . Secure Boot — ASRock X300TM-ITX Set this: Security → Secure Boot → Disabled Open the Security tab, then select the outlined Secure Boot entry. This screenshot shows the entry that opens its settings, not the on/off control itself. In the following screen, set Secure Boot to Disabled. The password rows are separate controls. This is the X300TM-ITX layout; check your model’s manual if it differs. Source: ASRock X300TM-ITX manual, printed page 47 . AMD SVM + IOMMU — ASRock X300TM-ITX Set this: SVM Mode → Disabled; IOMMU → Disabled Open Advanced → CPU Configuration. Change the first outlined row, SVM Mode, to Disabled. Then change IOMMU separately to Disabled. This source screenshot shows SVM Enabled and IOMMU Auto; neither is the target for this setup. PSS Support, NX Mode, SMT Mode and AMD fTPM switch are different settings. Source: ASRock X300TM-ITX manual, printed page 37 . Save changes — ASUS notebook Where to go: Save & Exit, or press F10 after completing all changes Set this: F10 → confirm Save & reset After completing all BIOS changes, save and confirm the restart. This ASUS example outlines OK; other models may call it Yes, Apply or Save Changes and Exit. Source: ASUS save-and-exit example . Names and locations for other BIOS layouts Show setting names and manufacturer menu locations Match the setting to your CPU and its purpose. Intel CPU virtualization and Intel I/O virtualization are separate controls; AMD SVM and IOMMU are separate too. A setting on Auto is not confirmation that it is off. Firmware labels you may encounter Setting Names to look for For this setup Intel CPU virtualization Intel Virtualization Technology, Intel (VMX) Virtualization Technology, Intel Virtualization Tech, VT-x, VMX Disabled Intel I/O virtualization VT-d, Intel VT-D Tech, VT for Direct I/O, Virtualization Technology for Directed I/O Disabled AMD CPU virtualization SVM Mode, SVM, Secure Virtual Machine, AMD-V Disabled AMD I/O virtualization IOMMU (may be separate from SVM) Disabled where available Secure Boot Secure Boot, Secure Boot Control, Secure Boot Enable; some ASUS models use OS Type Disabled; see ASUS note below Firmware fast boot Fast Boot; some boards offer a Fast Boot mode called Ultra Fast Disabled, rather than Fast or Ultra Fast Examples: ASUS Intel VMX , ASUS AMD SVM , Dell’s separate VT / Direct I/O controls , ASRock SVM / IOMMU example (PDF) , and ASRock Fast Boot modes . Where to look for virtualization controls ASUS Intel motherboards: Advanced Mode → Advanced → CPU Configuration → Intel (VMX) Virtualization Technology. ASUS documents F7 for switching to Advanced Mode on applicable boards. MSI Click BIOS: Advanced Mode → Overclocking → CPU Features → Intel Virtualization Tech / Intel VT-D Tech. MSI identifies the AMD equivalent as SVM Mode . Follow your model’s manual if the layout differs. MSI’s BIOS guide . Dell: look for a Virtualization or Virtualization Support page; CPU virtualization and Direct I/O may have separate switches. Lenovo: some ThinkPad models place these under Security → Virtualization. Lenovo’s virtualization guide . Other models: check Advanced, Security, Configuration or CPU Configuration. HP’s firmware-navigation guidance describes these common locations. The manufacturer pages explain how to find or enable virtualization. Use them to identify the control; the Plus setup here calls for it to be Disabled . ASUS: “Other OS” can be the Secure Boot control. On models covered by ASUS’s Secure Boot guide , Boot → Secure Boot → OS Type set to Other OS deactivates Secure Boot. This is not an instruction to switch the system to Legacy/CSM. Keep UEFI boot mode and verify Secure Boot State: Off in Windows after saving. A greyed-out state display may be read-only; look for the actual control. Common Secure Boot menu locations ASUS: Advanced Mode (F7) → Boot → Secure Boot. MSI: Settings → Advanced → Windows OS Configuration → Secure Boot. Gigabyte / Aorus: Boot → Secure Boot, or BIOS → Secure Boot. ASRock: Security → Secure Boot. Dell: Boot / Boot Sequence → Secure Boot. HP: Advanced → Secure Boot Configuration. Lenovo: Security → Secure Boot. Acer: Boot → Secure Boot. Surface / Framework: Security → Secure Boot. These are different settings: Hyper-Threading / SMT is not VT-x / SVM. TPM, Intel PTT and AMD fTPM are not virtualization switches. This setup does not call for clearing the TPM, deleting Secure Boot keys, changing storage settings such as AHCI / RAID / VMD, or loading BIOS defaults. Use Restart when applying the setup Firmware Fast Boot and Windows Fast Startup are different. Windows Fast Startup can preserve the kernel session after Shut down; Start → Power → Restart performs a full boot cycle. Use Restart after arming the driver or changing the Windows settings, rather than Shut down followed by power-on. See Microsoft’s explanation of Restart and Fast Startup . 6. Verify and load Scooby Plus Back in Windows, open msinfo32 . Confirm BIOS Mode: UEFI , Secure Boot State: Off , and VBS is not running. Confirm Memory Integrity is off and BitLocker decryption has completed. Open the Scooby loader and select GTA 5 . In Kernel protection , select Load Driver At Next Boot , then restart your PC . The supplied setup describes a Scooby bootloader / logo appearing during startup. A missing logo is a reason to check the driver status and setup, rather than proof of one specific failure. Sign back into Windows and open the Scooby loader. Press Load , then launch GTA V with BattlEye enabled . Open your menu interface: ClickUI: F1 / Insert . ListUI: F2 . Final checks after restarting System Information: msinfo32 should show BIOS Mode: UEFI , Secure Boot State: Off , and VBS not running. Unsupported is not the same result as Off; check the boot mode and ask support if that is what you see. CPU virtualization: open Task Manager → Performance → CPU and look for Virtualization: Disabled . This checks CPU virtualization; it does not separately confirm VT-d / IOMMU or Secure Boot. Confirm those in firmware. Memory Integrity: recheck Windows Security → Device security → Core isolation details after the restart. VBS / HVCI: run check_vbs.bat as administrator. A successful WMI result should report VBS running: 0 and HVCI running: 0 . If the source is REGISTRY or settings return, use the VBS troubleshooting guide . Encryption: an administrator terminal can run manage-bde -status C: to inspect conversion status and encryption percentage. For a fully decrypted Windows drive, look for Fully Decrypted and 0.0% ; Protection Off alone can mean suspension. Replace C: if Windows uses another drive letter. Microsoft’s status-command reference . The Kernel protection panel and Load Driver At Next Boot button. This reference image shows the driver before it is armed. Older loader wording may show a different launch order; use the current setup sequence above. Windows logo, boot hang or blue screen? Check the required settings and loader driver status. A hang or BSOD can also indicate a compatibility issue; do not assume every failure means the setup was done incorrectly. Open a support ticket with the exact error or stop code, Windows version, motherboard model and settings you changed. If Windows cannot boot, restore the previous firmware settings and use your recovery key if requested. For the red “Hypervisor / VBS is running” banner, continue to the diagnostic and troubleshooting guide . Missing settings or a different BIOS screen? Find your loader message Use the exact message or status shown by your current loader to choose the next step: EFI not armed Complete the requirements and final checks , then follow Load Driver At Next Boot and restart . Driver offline after restarting Recheck Secure Boot, firmware Fast Boot and virtualization, then capture the Kernel protection panel for support. The boot logo alone does not confirm the driver is available. Hypervisor / VBS is running Use the VBS/HVCI diagnostic guide . Include the full output when asking for help. The game opens, but the menu does not open Confirm the loader completed loading and click back into the game. Use F1 / Insert for ClickUI or F2 for ListUI . On keyboards that use F1 or F2 for media functions, check the keyboard’s Fn / function-key mode. The loader itself will not open or shows a runtime error Start with the Visual C++ runtime downloads and launcher troubleshooting . Record the exact error rather than changing more BIOS settings. I can only see an EZ / simplified screen Look for Advanced Mode or an on-screen mode-switch hint. Use the key shown by your firmware; F7 is common on the ASUS boards described above, but it is not universal. If the BIOS offers search, try the exact names in the setting-name reference . My AMD PC has no VT-x, or my Intel PC has no SVM That is expected: these labels belong to different CPU families. Use the Intel or AMD rows that match your processor. Not every device exposes a separate I/O virtualization switch, and a missing switch does not prove the feature is off. A setting is missing, locked or greyed out First confirm the exact PC / motherboard model and BIOS version. Check its manual and any dependency described there. Laptops, prebuilts and managed PCs can expose different controls from retail motherboards. Ask the manufacturer or support about a missing control rather than using an unrelated model’s instructions, unofficial BIOS unlocks or a guessed supervisor password. Do not flash a BIOS just because a tutorial’s menu looks different. The setting was changed, but Windows still reports the old value Re-enter firmware and confirm the change was saved. Use Save Changes and Exit, read the confirmation list, then restart and check Windows again. If firmware retains the change but VBS returns, check the Windows features and policy troubleshooting . If this begins after a BIOS update or reset, recheck the required settings before arming the driver again. I want to restore my usual security settings later Use the loader’s supported bootloader / driver removal procedure, or ask support for the current instructions, before restoring Secure Boot and the other recorded settings. Restart and verify Windows boots normally. Restore your usual encryption and security protections when you finish using this setup. What to include in a support ticket Send the exact PC or motherboard model, Intel/AMD processor, BIOS version, Windows version/build, a photo of the relevant BIOS screen, the loader’s Kernel protection status and any error or BSOD stop code. Include the diagnostic output if VBS is involved, and say which step you reached. Crop out recovery keys, passwords, account details and serial numbers before sharing. Copy a support-ticket template Fill in what you can check. Write “unknown” for anything you cannot confirm, and attach the relevant screenshots or diagnostic output separately. title: Themes
text: Themes Scooby themes can include colors, layout settings, backgrounds, and other image layers. A theme may be a single JSON file or a folder containing its settings and images. Theme folder and menu C:\scooby\GTA5\themes Settings → Appearance → Themes Use Open Themes Folder to open the correct location. Install Apply Save and share Troubleshooting Enlarge image ↗ Open Settings , then follow Appearance → Themes . The highlighted gear / Settings row is the starting point; the theme controls are described below. Enlarge image ↗ Folder-layout illustration, not a product screenshot. Copy the entire bundle; the filenames in your theme may differ. Install a downloaded theme Get a Scooby GTA 5 theme from its author or the Scooby community . Extract the archive first. Open Settings → Appearance → Themes → Open Themes Folder . For a single-file theme, copy the .json file directly into C:\scooby\GTA5\themes . For a theme bundle, copy the entire theme folder into themes . Keep its JSON and image files together, with the author's filenames and relative paths unchanged. Return to the menu and select Refresh Library . Example layouts (the image filenames in your download may be different): C:\scooby\GTA5\themes\ SimpleTheme.json MyTheme\ MyTheme.json background.png The theme JSON should sit at the top of its bundle folder. Avoid accidentally adding an extra wrapper folder when extracting a ZIP. Apply a theme to the interface you use Select the theme in the library. Choose Save / Load Scope : Both , ClickUI , or ListUI . Select Load Selected Theme . Check the status message and the chosen interface. Both applies the available settings for both interfaces. ClickUI or ListUI applies that interface and its shared appearance settings. The theme must contain settings for the scope you choose; a ClickUI-only theme cannot supply a ListUI design. Save, back up, and share your design Adjust the appearance settings and choose the scope you want to save. Enter a new custom theme name and select Save Current Theme . Scooby creates C:\scooby\GTA5\themes\YourTheme\YourTheme.json and bundles referenced images into the theme folder. Use Open Selected Folder to find the result. Back up or ZIP the entire folder when sharing it. Quick Save updates the selected custom theme. Use a new name when you want to keep the previous version. Built-in themes are protected from overwriting and deletion; save a custom copy to edit them. If the theme does not look right Not listed: extract the archive, check that the JSON is directly in themes or directly inside its bundle folder, clear the search, and refresh. Missing background or images: copy the complete bundle again. Sharing only its JSON can leave referenced images behind. Only one interface changes: check Save / Load Scope and the interfaces included in the theme. Load fails: restore the original JSON and confirm the theme supports your Scooby version. A theme from another menu is not automatically compatible. Want to undo a change: load a previously saved theme or a built-in theme from the library. Save your current design before experimenting if you want to keep it.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Troubleshooting Here are solutions to common issues you may encounter: Plus: Hypervisor / VBS is running Use the VBS/HVCI troubleshooting guide and check_vbs.bat download to identify the trigger. For Secure Boot, Fast Boot, driver loading or boot failures, start with the Plus Setup Guide . The BattlEye-disabled injection fixes below apply to the corresponding free / non-Plus loading path. For the Plus bootloader path, follow the Plus guide and keep BattlEye enabled. Failed to allocate memory in target process Head to your Rockstar Launcher, click on Settings, and disable BattlEye . This will fix the issue. Please return to Grand Theft Auto V (Black Screen) You must inject the menu during the loading screen. This message means the game is signifying you're going back to story mode. BattlEye is required to play GTA V Online Same solution - inject the menu during the loading screen, not when you're already in the game. Black screen with an error message Restart your game without opening Scooby and go to story mode before injecting. Frame Generator is now supported , so you no longer need to turn it off. Failed to write process memory Turn off BattlEye in the Rockstar Launcher settings. Launcher, free key & injection troubleshooting Follow this guide if the launcher closes after opening, the free key website is unreachable, injection fails, or injection succeeds but the menu does not work in game. Check your connection. Try a VPN, then retry the website or launcher. Your network or ISP may be blocking the connection. Clear the cache if the launcher still closes or injection fails. Close Scooby, delete the C:\scooby folder, then restart Scooby and try again. If injection still fails, check whether antivirus is blocking the loader. Follow the Antivirus & Download FAQ for the next steps. If only the free key website is affected, you do not need to reset the launcher cache. If the issue continues, contact support with the error message and the steps you have tried. Not listed here? See Universal Troubleshooting in the General tab - it covers "Failed to inject module", Auth Failed, crashing on inject, BattlEye kicks and the Scooby folder going missing. If Windows is flagging or deleting the loader, start with the Antivirus & Download FAQ .

title: Vehicles
text: Vehicles Saved Vehicles stores reusable vehicle presets. These files describe a vehicle and its saved settings; the underlying model must already be available in your game. Vehicle folder and menu C:\scooby\GTA5\vehicles Vehicle → Saved Vehicles → Browse in ClickUI and ListUI. Supported preset formats include .json , .xml , and .ini . Downloads Legacy / Enhanced Install Other-menu imports Save and share Troubleshooting Download vehicles Browse and download vehicles from Nenyoo ↗ Check the download’s file format and edition requirements before importing it. Extract the archive first, then use the installation steps below. Check Legacy / Enhanced compatibility Choose a download made for your game edition and a format Scooby supports. Addon models and textures may need conversion between Legacy and Enhanced; a saved preset does not perform that conversion. See addon edition and conversion help . Enlarge image ↗ Open Vehicle , then Saved Vehicles for downloaded presets. This Enhanced screenshot shows the spawner; the Saved Vehicles tab is outlined. Layouts can differ by menu version. Install and spawn a shared vehicle Download a compatible vehicle preset from Nenyoo vehicles or its author, and extract it if it is inside an archive. Open Vehicle → Saved Vehicles and select Open Folder , or paste C:\scooby\GTA5\vehicles into File Explorer. Copy the preset into the vehicles folder or your own subfolder. Keep the original extension. Open Browse , select Refresh , and open the folder containing the vehicle. Select the vehicle to spawn it. Enable Spawn Inside if you want to enter it automatically. 3D Preview shows a preview when one is available. C:\scooby\GTA5\vehicles\ MyVehicle.json Favorites\ SharedVehicle.xml Keep personal saves in the parent folder or your own subfolders. vehicles\PresetVehicles is used for bundled presets. Import a vehicle from another menu Place the original export in the matching folder: Stand: C:\scooby\GTA5\other-menu-addons\stand-vehicles Cherax: C:\scooby\GTA5\other-menu-addons\cherax-vehicles Other supported exports: C:\scooby\GTA5\other-menu-addons\other-menus-vehicles Open Other Menu / Other Menus in Saved Vehicles, refresh, and choose the import. Compatible .json , .txt , .ini , and .xml exports can be scanned. Keep files directly in the matching folder and preserve their original structure; an extension alone does not guarantee support. The installed format notes are in C:\scooby\GTA5\other-menu-addons\VEHICLES-GUIDE.txt . Save and share your own vehicle Enter the vehicle you want to save and finish customizing it. Open Vehicle → Saved Vehicles → Save Vehicle , or browse to the subfolder where you want to save. Choose JSON [SCOOBY] for a native Scooby save, XML [Menyoo] for a Menyoo-compatible export, or INI [Other Menus] for a supported INI export. Select Save Current Vehicle and enter a filename without an extension. Scooby adds the selected extension. Use Open Folder to copy, back up, or share the file. Include any model or edition requirements when sharing. Save as Personal Vehicle opens the garage registration flow. Use Save Current Vehicle when you want a portable file; saving a preset is separate from registering a personal vehicle. If a vehicle will not appear or spawn Missing preset: check the folder and extension, clear the search, open the correct subfolder, and refresh. Cannot save: enter a valid vehicle first and use a simple filename. Cannot spawn: the model may be unavailable in your game build, or the preset may use an unsupported structure. Restore the original download or ask for a compatible export. Wrong format: select the intended save format before saving. Changing .xml to .json does not convert the file. Downloaded an RPF or model assets: follow Addons . The saved-vehicle folder does not install custom game assets. Back up the vehicles folder and import folders while Scooby is closed. In ListUI, pressing Right on a local library entry permanently deletes that file.

title: Money, items & weapons
text: Money, items & weapons Money, items, weapons, and rewards depend on the server you are playing on. There is no universal trigger that works on every server. Reviewing server events Load into the server and wait for its resources to finish loading. Use the server dump feature, then review the dumped resources for events related to inventories, weapons, jobs, or rewards. Read the surrounding code to understand an event’s purpose and requirements. An event name alone does not tell you whether it will work. Why an event may not work Servers may validate these events on the server side. A request can be rejected if you do not meet the required conditions, such as being in the correct location, having the right job or permissions, or completing a task before claiming its reward. A server dump does not guarantee access to the server-side logic or reveal every validation check. Risk of a kick or ban Attempting to use a protected event may result in an immediate kick or ban, or may have no effect. Finding an event in a dump does not mean it is unprotected or safe to use. Server-specific support You are responsible for finding and understanding events for the server you use. Scooby does not provide server-specific money, item, weapon, or reward triggers, and support cannot help you find working triggers or bypass a server’s protections.
